text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- An editorial bitterly attacks OSCE and U.S. proposals to postpone elections in some areas, saying they serve President Sali Berisha's intention to divide Albania.
- Newspaper called into question an Italian-led multinational force, alleging they are sent as simple tourists.
- Violence hit the port town of Durres where five people were killed and several injured over the weekend.
- Leaders of the so-called committee of public salvation in Vlore warned President Berisha not to visit the town. Berisha will come under strong fire from every corner, they said.
- OSCE will spend some $5 million to monitor elections in Albania set for June 29.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE

- An armed group has forced Socialist Party Secretary General Rexhep Mejdani to cancel three rallies in the northern region of Puke. A group of 40 attackers shot at his car and his police escort but noone was injured.

- An OSCE spokesman said irregularities during Albania's June 29 elections are unavoidable. Up to 450 OSCE observers will be monitoring the vote and European Parliament member Catherine La Lumiere will prepare the final report.
- Albanian parties have launched an appeal to the government for more financing because their funds have dried up and they are relying on supporters' contributions.
- The U.S. National Democratic Institute has recommended postponing elections in some areas otherwise the whole voting process might fail.

- The deputy chairman of the Central Election Commission, has travelled to some towns of Albania's anarchic south to help solve problems ahead of the June 29 poll under an armed escort after the multinational escort refused to accompany him there.
- The Monarchy Party says 56 percent of Albanians will vote for a constitutional monarchy instead of a republic in the referendum on June 29.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Paper says promises by Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano that his party will pay back to Albanians the savings they lost in pyramid investment schemes is cynical and irresponsible.
- Thousands of Albanians threatened by famine.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- More than 20,000 enthusiastic supporters attended a rally of the Socialist Party in the southern town of Kucove where Prime Minister Bashkim Fino is a candidate.
- Socialist leader Fatos Nano has united Albanians against the dictator Berisha, paper says.
